items.title: Home
items.text:
Enable typer subcommands to inherit common options from their parent commands.

Do you ever get frustrated that flags defined on parent groups can't be set in child commands? I do! I hate having to write commands like my-app --verbose do thing when I want to write my-app do thing --verbose.

There are issues and discussions on the typer github repo talking about this missing feature, but I didn't find the solutions satisfying.

So, I made typer-scion.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
Typer lets a group callback declare options, but those options belong to the group. If you define a ---verbose option to the group to set up logging, then running app --verbose cmd works. However, running app cmd --verbose will fail with typer complaining about no such option. ltyper-scion lets you declare an option once, on a parent callback, and have any subcommand that opts in accept it too. Here's how:

  1. Mark an option with Inheritable() on the parent callback
  2. Opt a command in with @inherit
  3. Receive the value by name with Inherited(), as **kwargs, or from get_inherited()
  4. Inherited options appear in the child's --help, in their own panel

items.title: Features
items.text:
Every feature below has a runnable demo, and the examples directory of the repository holds complete scripts. The demo's --help lists the available features:

uvx --from typer-scion typer-scion-demo --help

items.title: Sharing an option
items.text: A parent callback shares an option by marking it with Inheritable() inside Annotated. The option stays an ordinary option of the group, so app --verbose cmd keeps working. Only commands decorated with @inherit receive it. Every other command behaves exactly like a plain Typer command.

items.title: Receiving options
items.text:
A command has three ways to receive inherited options:

  • By name. A parameter annotated Annotated[T, Inherited()] takes its default and option definition from the parent, so the child never repeats them.
  • As keyword arguments. A command that accepts **shared gets every inherited option in a dict.
  • From the context. Calling get_inherited() inside the command reads the values without touching the signature.

Typer merges inherited options into the command's signature, so they appear in --help under an "Inherited from ..." panel that names the ancestor sharing them.

items.title: Values flow both ways
items.text: A value given to the child on the command line also ascends to the parent. Once the child's options are parsed, the parent callback runs again with the child's value. Because of this re-invocation, parent callbacks that declare inheritable options work best when they are idempotent, which suits configuration such as logging.

items.title: Shadowing
items.text: A command can declare its own parameter with the same name as an inherited option. The command's declaration wins, much like a subclass attribute shadows its parent's, and the inherited option is simply not added.

items.title: Nested groups
items.text:
A command inherits from the app it is registered on. Options from higher groups reach it because each intermediate group callback is decorated with @inherit as well, and passes along whatever it inherits in turn.

A callback can both receive an option with Inherited() and share its own with Inheritable(). A few rules govern how the chain behaves:

  • When two groups declare the same name, the nearest group wins.
  • A group without a callback contributes nothing, so the search continues with its parent.
  • A group whose callback is not decorated with @inherit ends the chain, and groups above it stay out of reach.

items.title: Errors
items.text:
Misconfiguration surfaces as a ScionError, with a more specific subclass for each case:

  • UnknownInheritedOptionError appears when an Inherited() parameter matches no option shared by an ancestor.
  • InheritedDefaultError appears when an Inherited() parameter declares a default, since the parent supplies it.
  • InheritableOnCommandError appears when Inheritable() is used on a command instead of a group callback. Options flow downward through group callbacks only, so a command's options never reach its siblings.

items.title: Requirements
items.text: • Python 3.12 to 3.15

items.title: Installation
items.text:
This will install the latest release from pypi via uv:

uv add typer-scion

items.title: Using
items.text:
A typical app has two parts: a parent callback that shares an option, and a command that receives it.

  1. Declare the shared option on the parent callback and mark it with Inheritable().
  2. Decorate the command with @inherit, placed below @app.command().
  3. Annotate a parameter of the command with Inherited() to receive the value.
from typing import Annotated

import typer
from typer_scion import Inheritable, Inherited, inherit

app = typer.Typer()


@app.callback()
def main(verbose: Annotated[bool, typer.Option(), Inheritable()] = False): ...


@app.command()
@inherit
def work(verbose: Annotated[bool, Inherited()]):
    print(f"verbose={verbose}")

With that in place, app work --verbose works, and so does app --verbose work. The work command lists --verbose in its --help, and the option keeps the default and help text the parent gave it.

items.title: Run the demo
items.text:
The demo walks through each feature in an isolated environment with uv:

uvx --from typer-scion typer-scion-demo

Passing --help to the command shows the available options.

items.title: Inheritable
items.text:
Marker placed in Annotated metadata on a parent's option to make it shareable with subcommands.

A value given to a child on the command line also ascends to the parent callback that declared the option: once the child's options are parsed, the parent callback is invoked again with the child's value. (Typer runs a parent's callback before it looks at the subcommand's arguments, so a re-invocation is the only way for the parent to learn the child's value.) Parent callbacks that declare inheritable options should therefore be idempotent, which is natural for configuration like logging.

items.title: InheritableOnCommandError
items.text:
Bases: ScionError

Raised when Inheritable() is used on a command instead of a group callback.

Options are shared downward through group callbacks only. A command's own options are never visible to its siblings, and a command has no subcommands to receive them.

items.title: Inherited
items.text:
Marker placed in Annotated metadata on a child's parameter to receive an option shared by an ancestor.

The parameter carries no default and no option definition of its own: both come from the ancestor, and the option is listed in --help as inherited. UnknownInheritedOptionError is raised if no ancestor shares an option with that name. Example: def child(verbose: Annotated[bool, Inherited()]): ...

items.title: InheritedDefaultError
items.text:
Bases: ScionError

Raised when a parameter marked Inherited() also declares a default, since the default comes from the parent.

items.title: ScionError
items.text:
Bases: Buzz

Base class for all errors raised for invalid inheritance configuration.

items.title: UnknownInheritedOptionError
items.text:
Bases: ScionError

Raised when a parameter marked Inherited() names an option that no app in the chain shares.

items.title: get_inherited
items.text:
get_inherited(ctx: Context | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]

Return the inherited option values for the running command.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ctx Context | None

The context to read. Defaults to the current one.

None

Returns:

Type Description dict[str, Any]

The inherited options by name, or an empty dict if the command inherits none.
